details:
Cosmic Legacy is a browser-based 3D educational game prototype that explores the stories of NASA spacecraft and equipment left on the Moon. Players begin with a simulated Earth launch, select the Moon, and explore a simplified lunar environment using an astronaut character and scanner.

The first mission focuses on Apollo 11’s Eagle descent stage. Players collect five virtual reconstruction parts—landing legs, descent engine, fuel tank, ladder, and scientific equipment bay—and match each part to its function. Correct matches unlock educational chapters. Completing this mission unlocks Surveyor 3, where players recover virtual research records about its camera, soil scoop, and later visit by Apollo 12 astronauts.

The prototype uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Babylon.js to create interactive 3D scenes in a web browser. Its creative approach combines exploration, assembly puzzles, and historical storytelling to make space engineering easier to understand. The intended impact is to encourage curiosity about science, engineering, and the lasting legacy of space exploration.

Historical explanations distinguish facts from gameplay. The reconstruction parts are fictional learning objects, and the spacecraft models are simplified procedural recreations. Eagle’s descent stage remains on the Moon; its ascent stage carried the astronauts back to lunar orbit to rendezvous with Columbia.
